title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: Post-order DFS. Each node returns the best single-branch gain (clamped at 0); a global tracks the best left+node+right path seen at any node.

notes: Distinguish two things at each node: (a) the best path through it using BOTH children — only updates `best`, never returned; (b) the upward gain via ONE child — what you return to the parent.
Clamp each child gain at 0: a negative branch is better skipped than taken.
`best` must start at `-Infinity`, not 0 — paths can be entirely negative (e.g. tree [-3]).

questions.q: Why is each child's gain clamped at 0 with `Math.max(gain, 0)`?
options: Because a negative-sum branch is worse than not taking that branch at all

questions.q: What does the recursive function RETURN to its caller?
options: The best path through the current node using both children
The best single-branch upward gain from this node (node.val + max(left, right))
The sum of every node in the subtree
questions.explain: The caller can only extend the path via ONE side; the through-node path is closed and only updates `best`.

options: The tree could contain only negative values, so the answer can be negative
O(h) where h is tree height

exercises.prompt: Fill in the post-order recursion for max path sum.

blanks.hint: extend upward via the better single side

L3.prompt: Write `maxPathSum(root)` returning the maximum node-to-node path sum in a binary tree. Log `maxPathSum(root)` for the tree [-10, 9, 20, null, null, 15, 7].
hints: Helper `gain(node)` returns node.val + max(left, right), each child clamped at 0.
Update a closure-scoped `best` with node.val + left + right at every node.
